cycle.label: Reporting period
cycle.note: Florida CPE periods run July 1 – June 30, every two years.

requirements.label: Total CPE
requirements.note: Hours must be done by June 30. Proof must be uploaded to the DBPR On-Line Services portal by December 31 after the period, before your license renewal. Nonresidents may instead show their home state's CPE compliance, but still need the Florida ethics course.
requirements.warning: Missed June 30? Automatic extension to September 15 with 8 extra accounting & auditing hours (88 total), or to December 31 with 16 extra (96 total).

requirements.label: Behavioral
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 20 behavioral hours count toward the 80. Under the rule, anything that isn't accounting & auditing, technical business or Florida-approved ethics is behavioral — including communications, personal development and general (non-Florida) ethics courses.

requirements.label: Governmental (Yellow Book audits)
requirements.note: 24 hours of governmental CPE if you work on audits under Government Auditing Standards. This comes from the GAO Yellow Book, not the Florida rule.

requirements.label: Florida Board-approved ethics
requirements.note: 4 hours from a Florida Board-approved ethics provider, covering Chapters 455 and 473, F.S. We count courses with "Florida" and "ethics" (or "473") in the title — edit the title if yours isn't picked up.

newLicensee.note: Your first Florida CPE period runs from your license issue date to the third June 30 after it.

licenseDateHint: Florida CPE periods end June 30 every two years (e.g. 06/30/2027). This is separate from your license renewal date.
issueDateHint: If you were licensed recently, your first period runs from this date to the third June 30 after it.
limitsNotTracked: Self-study in A&A or technical business must be from NASBA QAS sponsors.
Authorship: max 20 hours per period, and never toward ethics.
Credit in increments of not less than one half hour (50-minute contact hour).
toVerify: Economics, Business Law and Statistics treated as technical business per the Board's CPE Guidelines ('general business'); the rule text itself doesn't name them.
Production (operations/supply chain) treated as behavioral under the rule's catch-all — conservative; confirm.
First period: full 80 hours from issue date to the third June 30 — the rule has no proration.
recordRetention: Keep proof for at least two years after each two-year period.
